grades.reason: Discusses I/O ordering and address-translation synchronization, not instruction-fetch synchronization after code writes.

grades.quote: the behavior of FENCE.I is described in Chapter 5
grades.reason: Provides a reference to FENCE.I semantics but no synchronization requirements.

grades.quote: FENCE.I was removed from the Linux user ABI and is problematic in implementations with large incoherent instruction and data caches. However, it remains the only standard instruction-fetch coherence mechanism.
grades.reason: Identifies FENCE.I as the instruction-fetch coherence mechanism without explaining when it is required.

grades.quote: Memory writes to the jump vector table require an instruction barrier ( _fence.i_ ) to guarantee that they are visible to the instruction fetch.
grades.reason: Directly specifies synchronization after modifying instruction-fetched jump-table entries, but does not cover executable-code writes generally.
